note: Contrarian Shark, skeptical-researcher angle. Judged only against the locked North Star surfaces. The draft restates five criteria, remaps them to four, then treats stub-green, best-effort writes, and skippable Playwright as if they identified the claim.

findings.section: Wave 4 — Hook B/C and HOLD P2.8
findings.criterion: 1 — When a Gandalf run finalizes, a researchPrime / lane job finishes, or a Foreman wave GOes, one row is appended
findings.message: Criterion 1 names three finish events. The third is not “Foreman finishes.” It is “a Foreman wave GOes.” The plan parks that trigger (P2.8, “NOT built by default — folded into Hook C”) and then excludes the build lane from Hook B (`lane in ('research', 'plan')` only). What remains is a commissioned RUN_DONE row for an execution log, once, if the session was steward-commissioned. A five-wave build that GOes four times and then dies never fires finish_run, so the register is empty for the whole life of the run — the opposite of the locked trigger. The risk row already decided the classic-window case (project root is the effort of record). Hook B refusing `build` plus P2.8 HOLD together leave that mitigation unimplemented. Re-asking “live per-wave or once at finish?” at the Stage-2 gate re-opens a lock. Wire the wave-GO row, or amend criterion 1. As written, the third trigger is neither implementable nor measured.

findings.topic: live proof uses old in-effort path
findings.criterion: 2 — a register row may point at an Anchor route, not only an in-effort file; 5 — a Gandalf run on a real project is opened from the plan outline AND the deliverables tile
findings.message: The Why Now is that the register already opens files inside the effort folder and fails on reports that live in lane output dirs and Gandalf run dirs. Wave 4 then states that a cockpit-commissioned Gandalf store IS the effort dir, so Where is the plain `gandalf/run-<id>/report.md` — today’s realpath containment, already a link. Wave 7 dogfoods exactly that path and asserts a click through to “Bottom line.” That screenshot can be taken on the current parser with classify_route never succeeding. The new Where forms the plan exists to add — `/artifact/<pid>?path=…` for an out-of-effort report, `/report/<pid>/<lane>/<job_id>` for a lane job — are not the live click. Criterion 2 is therefore identified by a source-level delivRow assertion (Wave 2) and never by the page criterion 5 names. A green W7 on a commissioned in-effort Gandalf does not falsify “skill reports still render as text.”

findings.criterion: 5 — Nothing regresses, and it is seen; the steward/cockpit nets stay green
findings.message: The machine-countable gate is `tests/test_steward_deliverables.py`, two pre-existing cockpit files, and `tests/test_reports_links_2026_09_05.py`. No wave creates `test_reports_links_2026_09_05.py`. The files the waves do emit — `test_register_routes_2026_09_05.py`, `test_deliverables_register_2026_09_05.py`, `test_run_deliverable_terminal.py`, `test_register_links_playwright_2026_09_05.py` — are absent from that command. Foreman either collection-fails on a missing file or, if someone adds an empty namesake, never runs the STUB GATE, the registrar concurrency/idempotency net, the Run allowlist, or the only page proof. Criterion 5’s “nets stay green” is then a count over the wrong tests. A gate that cannot emit counts for the claims it ships is not a gate.

findings.criterion: 5 — a Gandalf run opened from outline AND tile; a run: row opens a terminal with the command staged (Playwright screenshots), before v1.2.13
findings.message: Criterion 5 is a claim about the page, not about pytest staying green. The only surface proof is `tests/test_register_links_playwright_2026_09_05.py` with `pytest.importorskip('playwright')`, and that file is not in the plan test-command. importorskip means the steward/cockpit/terminal nets named in the same criterion can pass while Playwright never ran. The run: half plants a hand-written smoke row — it does not observe a finish hook writing `run:` — so a screenshot of a staged command does not identify criterion 1 and criterion 4 together. File-presence of a PNG is the v4 failure class this wave cites and then reimplements. Name a non-skippable ship rule that the two clicks and the unsent command are on the page, or criterion 5 remains a procedure.

findings.criterion: 2 — a Where cell that is /report/… or /artifact/… is openable; the pane and the plan outline render it as a link that opens in a new window
findings.message: Wave 1’s positive fixture is `/artifact/<pid>?path=gandalf/run-1/report.md` and the grammar forbids a second query key on the stored cell. Wave 2 then sets `href` to “the route plus the token appended exactly as the deliverable-file link does at :458–462.” File-link concatenation and a pre-formed `/artifact/…?path=` URL are not the same shape. Naive `?token=` on a route that already has `?path=` yields a URL the artifact handler will not open; `&token=` is a second query key the parser would reject if it were stored. The Wave 2 test (“href is the route plus the page token”) passes either join. No assertion requires a single well-formed query string that `/artifact/` accepts. Criterion 2’s “opens in a new window” is therefore not identified for the route form the Why Now actually needs.

findings.section: Wave 4 — Hook B and Hook C
findings.criterion: 1 — one row is appended when a run finishes; Double rows on retry/resume — registrar idempotent on (what, where)
findings.message: Idempotency is exact `(what, where)`. Hook B writes `/report/<pid>/<lane>/<job_id>` with a lane-job what-string. Hook C writes a different where (in-effort rel or `/artifact/…`) and a different what (`<skill> — <role>: <filename>`). The plan never states these finish points are mutually exclusive, and a commissioned researchPrime/Crucible run is the production path that can be both a lane job and a `finish_run`. Tests pin “`_finalize` twice” and “`finish_run` twice,” each hook against itself. They do not pin one commissioned finish → one row across both hooks. Two where values are two rows. Criterion 1’s count is then unmeasured on the steward path the elegance pass calls load-bearing.

findings.criterion: 1 — one row is appended when a run finishes
findings.message: Criterion 1 is a count: one row per named finish. Hook B obeys it (one `/report/` per job). Hook C does not: done-when is “exactly one row per human-facing doc.” A session with report + plan + execlog is three rows for one RUN_DONE. Idempotency on `(what, where)` cannot collapse that grain because each file is a different where. The North Star’s examples are a Gandalf report, a researchPrime plan or report, a Foreman execution log — one human artifact per finish, not a role map. The plan therefore cannot say what “one row” means on the commissioned path. Pick a grain — one row per finished run, pointing at the human artifact — and gate it; the blast is not that grain.

findings.criterion: 1 — when a run finalizes, one row is appended to the effort’s DELIVERABLES.md
findings.message: The Why Now is that listing a human artifact is a hope because nothing writes the row. The fix is a function that “never raises (best-effort, returns the reason)” plus a journal field `{register: written|dup|reason}` and “a registrar exception can never fail a finished run.” A successful Gandalf/lane/commission finish can therefore still leave DELIVERABLES.md unchanged, and the surface John reads (outline + tile) has no failure state — only a log line. Tests pin cancelled/failed → no row and duplicate → one row; they do not pin “STATUS_DONE + `written: false`” as a visible miss. Journaling a silent no-op makes the miss auditable, not true. Criterion 1 is not “we tried.” Until a successful run with a failed write is a failed surface (or a hard, retried write), the convention remains a hope with better logs.

findings.criterion: 4 — Run link opens a cockpit terminal with the command staged as a pending paste (Enter runs it); 5 — a run: row opens a terminal with the command staged
findings.message: The dependent variable is the command sitting unsent on the shell prompt so Enter runs it. The plan operationalizes “prompt” as “the PTY produced its first output bytes.” First bytes from `%COMSPEC%`/PowerShell are banner, profile, or a cwd warning — not `PS …>`. Flushing raw bytes into that stream (explicitly no bracketed paste, no trailing newline) can land the command in the middle of startup text; Enter then does not run the staged command as a unit, which is a failure mode the risk table (“never submits”) does not name. The stub PTY “emits immediately,” so the once-only / no-newline fixtures cannot see a real prompt. The 45-second greet fallback is removed as an auto-send hazard and not replaced, so a quiet shell never stages at all. Criterion 4 is identified against a stub that cannot fail the way the host shell fails.

findings.topic: outline join untested for route rows
findings.criterion: 3 argument is “stepDelivLine already calls delivRow … zero outline-side edits … hence in the deliverables tile and under its step.” The Given/When/Then claims a cockpit render of step 2’s expansion. The tests actually listed are API pass-through and a jsdom-free source scan for `innerHTML`. If stepDelivLine (or anything upstream) still filters on `it.path` / in-effort existence, route rows vanish from the outline while delivRow unit tests stay green. Wave 3 keys Step as a 1-based index of `status == 'active'`; that join is asserted against a synthetic map, not against `stepDelivLine`’s real key. Criterion 3 is a join on the page. This wave measures a renderer helper and a comment about reuse.

findings.criterion: 4 — Run link opens a cockpit terminal in an Anchor window, token-gated, killable
findings.message: Criterion 4 is the window. Wave 6 leaves the URL as a HOLD (“can window.open reach the existing standalone xterm page with session+token as-is? If yes, cut the alias”). That is an unclosed decision inside a wave this document calls Foreman-ready. The existing page is already served at `/zombie_terminal?session=&token=`; a second route to the same page retires nothing. Wave 7’s Playwright cannot be written until the href is locked, so the surface gate depends on a question the plan deferred. Lock the URL or cut the alias. Do not ship a HOLD as the Run window.

findings.topic: concurrency test is threads not processes
findings.criterion: 1 — one row is appended; Double rows on retry/resume — registrar idempotent on (what, where)
findings.message: The plan cites the WinError-5 cross-process replace race and claims durability via unique temp + `os.replace` under `WRITE_LOCK`. The emitted property gate requires temp + fsync + rename and “two real processes.” Wave 3 specifies no fsync and tests “two-thread register → one row.” Threads in one process do not identify the incident the unique tmp name exists for, and they cannot see a torn replace across two finish hooks in two processes. Idempotency under the lock they share is a different claim. The durability story and the test measure different machines.
